Buwrt/githup.description: githup is a lightweight third-party GitHub client for Android, about 350 KB in size. It uses a WebView to host a front-end app with native-layer extensions, and supports repository browsing, Issue/PR handling, Actions viewing, Release publishing, full-page translation, and cloud APK packaging. It also includes a silent update mechanism and a five-layer security system.
Buwrt/githup.body:
# githup

A third-party GitHub client for Android. The `hup` in the name is **hub**, which is your GitHub in your pocket.

Technically, it's a bit interesting: **a WebView hosts a pure front-end single-page application, and the native layer only handles what the web can't do**, such as bypassing cross-origin restrictions for network requests, using the system file picker, binary uploads, and downloading and launching the installer. As a result, the whole thing is compressed to **around 350 KB**, yet it covers browsing repositories, viewing Issues / PRs, checking Actions, publishing Releases, uploading files, and even having GitHub Actions in the cloud build an APK for you.

What changed in each version is recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Buwrt/githup/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md) (starting from v1.1.3).

When the app opens, it automatically compares itself with this repository to check whether it is the latest version: **if it is already the latest, it stays completely silent and shows no reaction at all; only when a new version exists does it remind you, according to version-number rules.** You can also publish a new build without changing the version number. Upload the new package and update the checksum, and users will see a prompt the next time they open the app. The comparison is based on the package fingerprint, not just the version number. For detailed rules, see [Update mechanism](https://github.com/Buwrt/githup#更新机制).

> This app is a third-party client for personal learning purposes and is not affiliated with GitHub, Inc. All data is obtained through GitHub's official public API, and access tokens are stored only on your device.

|---|---|
| **Download** | [Latest Releases](https://github.com/Buwrt/githup/releases/latest) |

# blindcrate

🚀 blindcrate —— Four-player sealed auction · five-round blind bidding · blind-box unboxing battles. All bids are kept secret from the table, and players compete for a cabinet of unknown collectibles through clues, skills, and acting.

## 📖 Project Introduction

**blindcrate** is a multiplayer sealed-bid auction platform centered on "unknown collectibles." Each game has four players and five rounds of sealed bidding. You cannot see anyone's bids. You can only guess what the cabinet is worth from clues unlocked round by round, character-specific intelligence skills, and the hesitation each opponent shows when raising their paddle. The real tension begins after the gavel falls: the collectibles are revealed one by one from the fog, and you might uncover a family heirloom or end up with a pile of junk. The one who laughs last is the person who can both calculate accurately and fool others.

### ✨ Key Features

- 🎁 **Core unboxing loop** — priced in three tiers: free quota / tickets / points; weighted draws using weight × quality multiplier, with 7 quality tiers (grey · green · blue · purple · red · gold · prismatic)
- 🔐 **Safe grid search** — minable grid boxes with shape packing (`WxH`); search time is graded by quality, with "loss-protection" payouts
- 🧠 **Memory scan (vmem)** — 18×18 large grid card-flipping, 8 search chances, four interference types (quality drift / coordinate swap / phantom cells / signal blur), and three counter-items
- ⚔️ **Multiplayer safe auction** — 2 players 4 rounds / 4 players 6 rounds, `confirm → reveal → bidding → revealed` phase machine, forced buy (1.8×) and last-second bidding
- 🤖 **Humanlike AI opponents** — three information-utilization levels (0 / 45 % / 100 %), three personalities, and planned bids that round and snipe the way humans do
- 🎯 **Skill game** — 17 built-in skills, 17 effect types across four families (information / interference / modifier / tactics), double-click to equip, plus per-game usage limits
- 📚 **Catalog and collection** — rewards for completing each quality tier; names of uncollected items are masked to avoid spoilers; server-wide collection leaderboard
- 💳 **Monthly cards / pass / tasks** — three monthly card tiers (stackable discounts and ticket waivers), a 30-level season pass, and a daily and weekly task engine
- 🎪 **Live events** — check-in, limited-time drops, lottery-ticket wheel, loot-coin exchange, red-packet physical prize claims, and card-key pools
- 🧩 **Buff system** — quality multiplier, coin multiplier, drop weight, extra attempts, and battle ticket waivers, with bucketed value rules that prevent stacking cards
- 🛡️ **Engineering foundation** — unified response format, error code conventions, full Swagger docs, indexed tables without foreign keys, conditional-update deductions, Redis distributed locks

ceer-quant/BlitzkriegBot.body:
# BlitzkriegBot

### Turn trading ideas into runnable strategies.

Create strategies with a visual blueprint or Lua, validate them in backtesting and simulation environments, and manage accounts and risk through a panel.

**[Start simulating](#quickstart) · [Create your first strategy](#blueprint) · [View validation scope](https://github.com/ceer-quant/BlitzkriegBot/blob/HEAD/docs/FEATURES.md)**

*From node wiring to Lua strategy packages, make trading logic visible and easy to change.*

Defaults to dry simulation mode, and strategies are installed disabled by default. Live trading involves real financial risk and requires thorough validation and explicit authorization. This project does not constitute investment advice.

## Start from an idea

**Create strategy → Backtest and evaluate → Run in simulation → Go live once validation and authorization conditions are met**

| What you want to do | How to do it in BlitzkriegBot |
| --- | --- |
| Write the idea as rules | In the Blueprint, connect data sources, conditions, and actions; write Lua when you need more flexible logic. |
| Check whether a strategy is worth pursuing | Use the supported replay and backtest entry points to evaluate historical performance, and verify fees, drawdown, and fill assumptions. |
| Watch how it runs | Enable it per account in dry mode, and review orders, positions, ledger, and rejection reasons. |
| Decide whether to go live | Complete validation against feature evidence and venue constraints, then grant explicit authorization. Simulated profit is not a guarantee of live returns. |

## Blueprint: build your first strategy

Open the blueprint page, select inputs, conditions, guard logic, and actions from the node panel, and connect them into a rule:

```text
Data source / constant → Condition comparison → AND / OR combination → Buy / Sell / Hold
```

1. **Build the logic**: drag in nodes, connect ports, and adjust parameters in the properties panel.
2. **Check the output**: review the generated Lua and compile result. A successful compile means the code loads, not that the strategy is valid.
3. **Save and trial-run**: save as a strategy package, select an account on the strategy page, enable it in dry mode, and observe the results.

Blueprints support JSON import and export. Hand-written Lua packages can also be opened in source mode and edited further.

## One strategy package, validated step by step

Strategy packages can be reused across supported replay, simulation, and live entry points, which reduces the burden of maintaining multiple strategy implementations. The core accounting path has a dry/live reconciliation gate, and the validation scope can be reviewed in the [feature evidence table](https://github.com/ceer-quant/BlitzkriegBot/blob/HEAD/docs/FEATURES.md).

**Reusing code does not mean reproducing the market.** Live trading is still affected by liquidity, slippage, fees, network latency, and venue rules. Offline tests, dry-mode live observation, and partial real-order validation each cover different scopes and cannot replace full live acceptance.

librecapsula/capsula-userspace-jailbreak.body:
# capsula-jb — root on VK Capsula speakers via userspace overwrite

Jailbreak of VK Capsula (Rockchip RK3308) by overwriting userspace: the **userdata partition is not signed** and can be freely overwritten by the user. We place an overlay with the factory `adbd` into it, and after a reboot the speaker shows up as an ADB device (`2207:0006`): `adb shell` gives **root without authorization**. Other partitions are not modified, and the stock firmware keeps working as is.

Supported boards: **Capsule-14, Capsule-15**, and **first-generation speakers** ("gift" ones). The loader for Capsule-14/15 is the same: the signed usbplug from the Capsule-14 OTA (this is the same build in all current rk3308 firmwares). It is **embedded in the binary** (`resources/loader/loader.bin` in the repository), so the tool does not need network access. First-generation speakers are signed with a different key: their BootROM rejects our usbplug, so a full backup cannot be made on them. The tool detects them on its own (by the serial number of the stock u-boot: on regular speakers it starts with four digits, on first-generation ones with arbitrary hex characters) and offers to flash a freshly built userdata with the overlay right away, without a backup (see "First generation").

# IOTA Watch

An open-source, five-language, multi-project monitoring dashboard centered on **IOTA Train at Home**. It supports IOTA, XID / MMM, Quantus, fly.ai, Nosana, Gonka, Akash, io.net, Vast.ai and Golem; each project's inputs, cycles, and data coverage are described separately.

**[Official site](https://iotahome.site) · [My Devices](https://iotahome.site/zh/devices) · [IOTA Lookup](https://iotahome.site/zh/app) · [Network Status](https://iotahome.site/zh/network) · [Blog](https://iotahome.site/zh/blog) · [English](https://iotahome.site/en)**

IOTA Watch is an independent MIT-licensed monitor in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean and Japanese. IOTA Train at Home (Macrocosmos / Bittensor SN9) is the core project, with ten project pages covering training, mining and compute. Tool pages query records; separate tutorials explain identifiers, fields and troubleshooting. Public projects use public identifiers; io.net and Vast.ai require account connections with read credentials. Those two integrations have mocked validation; real-account validation remains pending.

The screenshot shows miner distribution and network capacity; the figures are official data as of when the screenshot was taken.

## Features

- **Multi-device monitoring**: add, name, and view devices by public Miner ID, filtering by contributing, waiting for tasks, needs checking, and pending confirmation.
- **Earnings records**: today, cumulative, paid, pending payment, frozen, and minimum payment amounts; also shows USD valuations with source and timestamp.
- **Training history**: view training tokens, throughput, and cumulative tokens by day, week, or month; missing data is left as gaps.
- **Network visualization**: regional distribution donut chart, miner count rankings, slot occupancy, task progress, and tier overview.
